data.content_ref: inline:ABSTRACTION: The problem of safe resumption after token-budget exhaustion abstracts the five foundation artifacts into a single decision predicate R = (L1 ∧ L2), where L1 = no committed event was modified or deleted (trivially preserved by append-only framing) and L2 = the resumed stream produces the same event sequence as uninterrupted execution. Each SRC artifact is a partial specialization: SRC_001 contributes the barrier as a sufficient L2 mechanism, SRC_002 contributes downstream-projection divergence as an L2 failure mode, SRC_004 contributes causally-atomic-step interruption as another L2 failure mode, and SRC_005 contributes side-channel leakage as the general L2 failure mode that subsumes SRC_002 and SRC_004. The isolated problem inherits this unified predicate. REFUTED IF: the causal fingerprint cannot be decomposed into independently verifiable L1 and L2 components—e.g., if the fingerprint is embedded in event payloads and a partial fragment corrupts the payload of the last complete event, making L1 and L2 observationally inseparable.
